steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Roman army was the most effective military force in the ancient world, enabling Rome's imperial expansion

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A legion consisted of approximately 5,000-6,000 soldiers divided into ten cohorts

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Each cohort had six centuries of 80 men commanded by a centurion

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Legionaries were Roman citizens who served 25 years; auxiliaries were non-citizens who gained citizenship on discharge

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Why was Roman discipline so effective? | Q: What was the difference between legionaries and auxiliaries? | Q: Why was the Roman marching camp important?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Strict training created instinctive obedience and cohesion. Decimation deterred cowardice. The marching camp imposed order. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Link military organisation to Rome's imperial success Use specific technical terms: legion, cohort, century, pilum, testudo The marching camp shows how discipline and engineering supported military power Compare the Roman army with other ancient armies to show what made it unique The army was a social institution — it integrated provinces and created citizens
